# Antes de ejecutar

Primero de cuatro QMD. Produce las Tables 1 y 2 del manuscrito, asociaciones
de una covariable, probabilidades de respuesta y comparación modal/BCH
(Table S2 del manuscrito). La Table 3 actual se produce en la etapa 02.
Las etiquetas históricas se conservan para reconstruir resultados;
su revisión conceptual se explica en `OBSERVACIONES_ANSOLEAGA.md`.

Entrada: archivo general **ya procesado**, mediante `LCA_RAW_PATH`, la
carpeta privada `datos/` o el archivo del proyecto padre. Se reutiliza
medición guardada únicamente después de verificar los ítems y sus filas.
`LCA_REFIT=1` solicita ajustar de nuevo 2–10 clases y el BLRT (costoso).
Salida principal: `salidas/01_general.RData`, objeto único `general`.
Los CSV conservan sus nombres históricos; su numeración no siempre coincide
con el manuscrito. Véase `MAPA_MANUSCRITO.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: directorio
dir.create("salidas", showWarnings = FALSE)
if (Sys.getenv("LCA_REFIT", "0") != "1" &&
    !file.exists("salidas/lca_results.rds") &&
    file.exists("../lca_results.rds")) {
  stopifnot(file.copy("../lca_results.rds", "salidas/lca_results.rds"))
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("salidas", winslash = "/"))
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: "hold"

rm(list = ls()); gc()

required_packages <- c(
  # data wrangling
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "purrr", "readr", "haven", "forcats", "stringr", "janitor", "rlang",
  # latent class analysis
  "glca", "poLCA",
  # survey-weighted estimation + simulation
  "survey", "MASS",
  # parallel backend for the enumeration fits + bootstrap LRT
  "future", "furrr",
  # multinomial logit (used for checks)
  "nnet",
  # plotting
  "ggplot2", "patchwork", "scales",
  # tables / output
  "knitr", "kableExtra", "digest"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages)) stop("Install required R packages before rendering: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
invisible(lapply(required_packages, function(pkg)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(pkg, character.only = TRUE))))
source("../R/leadership_table2.R")
source("../R/load_leadership_results.R")
source("../R/association_models.R")  # derive_psychotrop_flexible(), shared with 03/05
reuse_measurement <- file.exists("lca_results.rds") && Sys.getenv("LCA_REFIT", "0") != "1"
saved_measurement <- if (reuse_measurement) readRDS("lca_results.rds") else NULL
render_started_utc <- format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE)

set.seed(2125)            # 2125 = lucky seed; used for every stochastic step
options(scipen = 999)

## Random starting values for every glca() measurement fit (local-maxima
## safeguard). The reported models below use this many random starts; the
## bootstrap LRT (gofglca) is unaffected -- it warm-starts each replicate from
## the fitted parameters with a single EM run. Lower n_init (e.g. 50) for quick
## drafts and restore 4000 for the final, reportable run.
n_init <- 4000
```

## Data and variable mapping

The `vars` list maps analysis names to verified columns in the supplied file.
Required columns and positive survey weights are checked before estimation. Leadership items are the ordinal variables
`lid_des1 … lid_des14` (1 = never … 4 = almost always/always), of which **13**
enter the LCA — item 3 (`lid_des3`) is excluded.

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| results: "hold"

## (i) ------------------------------------------------------------ FILE PATH
## Resuelve la ruta automaticamente detectando la letra de unidad de Google
## Drive: prueba H:, G: y C: y usa la primera raiz donde el archivo exista.
## Asi el .qmd no se rompe si Google Drive cambia de unidad o se abre en otro PC.
## Solo mantienes 'rel' (ruta RELATIVA a la raiz de Google Drive).
read_any <- function(path) {
  switch(tolower(tools::file_ext(path)),
    dta = haven::read_dta(path),
    sav = haven::read_sav(path),
    rds = readRDS(path),
    csv = readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE),
    stop("Extension no soportada: ", tools::file_ext(path)))
}
## La base .rds se genero (en otra sesion) con:
##   rio::export(BD_2020_input3_match_not_miss, "BD_2020_input3_match_not_miss.rds")
raw_path <- Sys.getenv("LCA_RAW_PATH", "")
if (!nzchar(raw_path)) {
  candidates <- c("../datos/BD_2020_input3_match_not_miss.rds",
                  "../../BD_2020_input3_match_not_miss.rds")
  raw_path <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)][1]
}
if (is.na(raw_path)) stop("Supply the processed general input with LCA_RAW_PATH.")
raw_path <- normalizePath(raw_path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
if (!file.exists(raw_path)) stop("LCA_RAW_PATH does not point to an existing input file.")
## Alternativas (bases procesadas en la carpeta del proyecto), si las prefieres:
# raw_path <- resolve_drive_path("DOCUMENTOS/6.TESIS 2018/LCA NAQ/culorg 06-04- BD_05_02_19 (BD_22_10_18_lab_cul_org2)_post modelos_finales2.dta")
message("Datos cargados desde: ", raw_path)

raw <- read_any(raw_path) |> janitor::clean_names()   # LID_DES1..14 -> lid_des1..14

## (ii) ----------------------------------------------------- VARIABLE MAPPING
## Mapeo a las columnas REALES de BD_2020_input3_match_not_miss.rds. Las
## covariables vienen como FACTORES con etiquetas; abajo se construyen copias
## limpias: binarias 0/1 con 1 = expuesto (segun `yes_levels`) y continuas
## numericas (`cont_vars`). 'vars' solo documenta la columna de origen.
vars <- list(
  ## 13 leadership items (ordinal 1-4), CDLS item order lid_des1..14 with
  ## item 3 (lid_des3) EXCLUDED. lid_des3 -- "steers away from showing concern
  ## about results" -- is the negatively worded laissez-faire item; it is dropped
  ## from the LCA measurement model here, so 13 items enter every fit/figure.
  items  = paste0("lid_des", c(1:2, 4:14)),

  ## survey design
  weight = "weight",   # ponderador (continuo)
  strata = NA,         # no hay estrato muestral en esta base -> diseno solo-pesos
  psu    = NA,         # no hay conglomerado/PSU en esta base

  ## covariates for Tables 2 / S1-S3 (binary unless noted)
  age            = "a53",                  # CONTINUOUS: edad en anios (20-83)
  job_sat        = "satis",                # CONTINUOUS: suma satisfaccion laboral (0-20)
  sex_woman      = "a52",                  # 1 = "Women"
  eri            = "desbalance_dic",       # 1 = "Yes" (Effort-Reward Imbalance, ERI)
  naq_frequent   = "naq_a",                # 1 = "2" (cumple criterio Agervold de actos negativos)
  bully_self     = "autonaq",              # 1 = "Yes" (self-labeling bullied, 6m)
  sex_harass     = "acos_sex",             # 1 = "2" (acoso sexual, 12m)
  auditc_hazard  = "auditc",               # 1 = "Yes" (AUDIT-C de riesgo)
  no_union       = "org_sind",             # 1 = "Yes" (ausencia de sindicato)
  unpaid_care    = "carga_dom",            # 1 = "Yes" (cuidados no remunerados)
  no_secondary   = "educacion_media",      # 1 = "Yes" (no completo secundaria)
  small_wp       = "tamano_de_la_empresa", # 1 = "1 to 10" (lugar de 1-10 personas)
  customer_no    = "atpub",                # 1 = "Job w/o customer-facing tasks"
  econ_narrow    = "estrechez"             # 1 = "2" (estrechez economica)
)

## Covariables continuas (se copian como numericas, sin dicotomizar)
cont_vars <- c("age", "job_sat")

## Para cada covariable binaria: nivel(es) de texto que corresponden a "1 = expuesto".
## (Asi la direccion 0/1 queda explicita y auditable, sin depender del codigo 1/2.)
yes_levels <- list(
  sex_woman     = "Women",
  eri           = "Yes",
  naq_frequent  = "2",
  bully_self    = "Yes",
  sex_harass    = "2",
  auditc_hazard = "Yes",
  no_union      = "Yes",
  unpaid_care   = "Yes",
  no_secondary  = "Yes",
  small_wp      = "1 to 10",
  customer_no   = "Job w/o customer-facing tasks",
  econ_narrow   = "2"
)

## Build the analysis data frame -----------------------------------------
## Leadership items -> ordered factors with the SAME 4 levels (1..4).
## OJO: en esta base los items vienen codificados 0..3 (0 = nunca ... 3 = casi
## siempre/siempre). El resto del notebook asume 1..4, asi que se desplazan +1
## automaticamente si la base esta en base 0. (NO usar las versiones *_rec, que
## estan dicotomizadas 0/1, ni *_clus.)
required_columns <- unique(unlist(vars[!names(vars) %in% c("strata", "psu")]))
missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(raw))
if (length(missing_columns)) stop("Missing mapped columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
d <- raw
d$.source_row <- seq_len(nrow(d))
item_min <- suppressWarnings(min(vapply(vars$items,
              function(it) min(as.numeric(d[[it]]), na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))))
shift <- if (is.finite(item_min) && item_min == 0) 1L else 0L
for (it in vars$items) {
  values <- as.numeric(d[[it]]) + shift
  if (any(!is.na(values) & !values %in% 1:4)) stop("Invalid ordinal codes in ", it)
  d[[it]] <- factor(values, levels = 1:4, ordered = TRUE)
}
if (shift == 1L) message("Items de liderazgo recodificados de 0-3 a 1-4 (+1).")

## --- helpers de coercion ------------------------------------------------
## Numerico robusto: sirve para factor-de-numeros y para labelled/numeric.
as_num <- function(x) {
  if (is.factor(x)) return(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x))))
  as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(x))
}
## Binaria 0/1 desde un factor: 1 = nivel(es) en 'yes'. Los niveles de texto
## "NA"/"Not Apply" se tratan como perdidos (NA), no como 0.
to01 <- function(x, yes) {
  f <- as.character(haven::as_factor(x))
  f[f %in% c("NA", "Not Apply", "NaN", "")] <- NA
  if (!any(f %in% yes, na.rm = TRUE)) stop("No mapped exposed level found: ", paste(yes, collapse = ", "))
  out <- as.integer(f %in% yes)
  out[is.na(f)] <- NA_integer_
  out
}

## Continuas -> copia numerica
for (nm in cont_vars) d[[nm]] <- as_num(d[[ vars[[nm]] ]])
## Binarias -> copia 0/1 (1 = expuesto)
for (nm in names(yes_levels)) d[[nm]] <- to01(d[[ vars[[nm]] ]], yes_levels[[nm]])
## Psicofarmacos (2026-10-18): uso regular en 12 meses de ansioliticos, hipnoticos o
## antidepresivos; misma funcion y codigos que 03 (1 = no, 2 = si, 3 = nr).
psychotrop_items <- c("a46_top_1", "a46_top_12", "a46_top_13")
d$psychotrop_flexible <- derive_psychotrop_flexible(d, psychotrop_items,
                                                    yes = 2, no = 1, missing_codes = 3)

## Survey weights are required; silently replacing them with 1 changes the estimand.
d$.w <- as_num(d[[vars$weight]])
if (any(!is.finite(d$.w) | d$.w <= 0)) stop("Survey weights must be finite and positive.")

## Keep complete cases on the 13 items AND on the measurement-model concomitant
## (sex_woman, used as ~sex_woman in item_f). glca does listwise deletion on its
## model frame, so if the concomitant had any NA, g4$posterior would have FEWER
## rows than d_lca and post4/modal4 would silently misalign with d_lca, the survey
## design and every covariate vector. Enforcing it here keeps everything aligned.
concomitant <- "sex_woman"   # RHS of item_f in the enumeration chunk
d_lca <- d[stats::complete.cases(d[, c(vars$items, concomitant)]), ]
cat("Rows total:", nrow(d), " | complete on 13 items + ", concomitant, ":", nrow(d_lca), "\n")
model_input_hash <- digest::digest(d_lca[, c(vars$items, concomitant), drop = FALSE], algo = "sha256")
measurement_validation <- if (reuse_measurement)
  validate_saved_measurement(saved_measurement, d_lca, vars$items, concomitant) else "Fresh measurement estimation."
cat(measurement_validation, "\n")
sample_flow <- tibble::tibble(
  stage = c("Input records", "Complete on 13 leadership items", "Complete on 13 items and sex"),
  n = c(nrow(d), sum(complete.cases(d[, vars$items])), nrow(d_lca)))
```

```{r}
#| label: survey-design
#| results: "hold"

## Survey design for the weighted descriptives (Table 2).
## If strata/psu are not available, a weights-only design is used.
has <- function(k) !isTRUE(is.na(vars[[k]])) && vars[[k]] %in% names(d_lca)

if (has("strata") && has("psu")) {
  dsn <- svydesign(ids = as.formula(paste0("~", vars$psu)),
                   strata = as.formula(paste0("~", vars$strata)),
                   weights = ~.w, data = d_lca, nest = TRUE)
} else {
  dsn <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~.w, data = d_lca)
}
dsn
```

## Helper functions

`relative_entropy()`, the classification matrix, **BCH** weights, and the
from-scratch **ML three-step** estimator.

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| results: "hold"

## Relative entropy (0-1; higher = cleaner separation) from the posterior matrix.
relative_entropy <- function(post) {
  post <- as.matrix(post)
  n <- nrow(post); K <- ncol(post)
  e <- -sum(post * log(pmax(post, 1e-12)))
  1 - e / (n * log(K))
}

## Classification matrix D[t, w] = P(W = w | X = t), W = modal class.
class_matrix <- function(post, modal) {
  K <- ncol(post)
  ind <- outer(modal, 1:K, `==`) * 1            # n x K modal indicators
  A <- t(as.matrix(post)) %*% ind               # K x K : sum_i post[i,t] I(W=w)
  A / rowSums(A)                                 # rows (true t) sum to 1
}

## ---- BCH set-up: weight matrix bch[i, t] = (D^{-1})[t, w_i] -------------
## Bias-adjusted class statistics use column t of `bch` as weights.
bch_setup <- function(post, modal) {
  D <- class_matrix(post, modal)
  Dinv <- solve(D)
  bch <- t(Dinv[, modal])                        # n x K ; bch[i,t]=Dinv[t,w_i]
  list(D = D, Dinv = Dinv, w = bch)
}

## Bias-adjusted (BCH) weighted mean of a numeric x within each latent class.
## (Use for proportions of 0/1 variables and for the mean of a score.)
bch_class_mean <- function(x, bchw, sw = NULL) {
  x <- as.numeric(x); K <- ncol(bchw)
  if (is.null(sw)) sw <- rep(1, length(x))
  vapply(seq_len(K), function(t) {
    w <- bchw[, t] * sw
    sum(w * x, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(w[!is.na(x)])
  }, numeric(1))
}

## Naive (modal-assignment) mean of x within each class.
naive_class_mean <- function(x, modal, sw = NULL, K = max(modal)) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  if (is.null(sw)) sw <- rep(1, length(x))
  vapply(seq_len(K), function(t) {
    idx <- which(modal == t)
    sum(sw[idx] * x[idx], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(sw[idx][!is.na(x[idx])])
  }, numeric(1))
}

## ---- ML three-step (Vermunt 2010) for ONE covariate z ------------------
## Maximises  prod_i sum_t pi_t(z_i;b) * P(W=w_i | X=t),  reference class = 1.
## Returns coefficients, vcov, and per-class odds ratios (exp of the slope).
ml3step <- function(z, post, modal, sw = NULL, D = NULL) {
  post <- as.matrix(post); K <- ncol(post)
  if (is.null(sw)) sw <- rep(1, nrow(post))
  ## Classification matrix D[t,w]=P(W=w|X=t) is a FIXED property of the
  ## measurement step: compute it ONCE on the FULL sample (all rows of
  ## post/modal), BEFORE dropping NA on z. Computing it on the per-covariate
  ## complete-case subset would give each covariate a different D and would
  ## disagree with the BCH analysis (Table S3, which uses the full-sample D).
  if (is.null(D)) D <- class_matrix(post, modal)  # K x K, full measurement sample
  z <- as.numeric(z)
  ok <- !is.na(z)
  z <- z[ok]; modal <- modal[ok]; post <- post[ok, , drop = FALSE]; sw <- sw[ok]
  n <- length(z)   # rows AFTER dropping NA on z; must match z/sw or negll's
                   # outer(rep(1, n), a) is non-conformable when z has missings.
  Dw <- t(D[, modal])                            # n x K ; [i,t]=P(W=w_i|X=t)
                                                 # global D indexed by the subset modal
  negll <- function(par) {
    a <- c(0, par[seq(1, 2 * (K - 1), 2)])       # intercepts (a_1 = 0)
    b <- c(0, par[seq(2, 2 * (K - 1), 2)])       # slopes     (b_1 = 0)
    eta <- outer(rep(1, n), a) + outer(z, b)     # n x K
    eta <- eta - apply(eta, 1, max)              # stabilise
    pis <- exp(eta); pis <- pis / rowSums(pis)   # n x K class probs
    pw <- rowSums(pis * Dw)                       # P(W=w_i)
    -sum(sw * log(pmax(pw, 1e-12)))
  }
  fit <- optim(rep(0, 2 * (K - 1)), negll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
  V <- tryCatch(solve(fit$hessian), error = function(e) matrix(NA, length(fit$par), length(fit$par)))
  b_idx <- seq(2, 2 * (K - 1), 2)
  b  <- fit$par[b_idx]
  se <- sqrt(diag(V))[b_idx]
  tibble::tibble(
    class = 2:K,
    OR    = exp(b),
    lo    = exp(b - 1.96 * se),
    hi    = exp(b + 1.96 * se)
  ) -> ors
  list(par = fit$par, V = V, K = K, ors = ors, conv = fit$convergence)
}

## Parametric-bootstrap marginal predicted probabilities P(X=t | z) at z=0 and
## z=1, with 95% CIs and the difference (pp). Draws beta ~ N(beta_hat, V).
ml3step_margins <- function(m, B = 2000) {
  K <- m$K; par <- m$par; V <- m$V
  draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(B, mu = par, Sigma = V)
  probs <- function(p, z) {
    a <- c(0, p[seq(1, 2 * (K - 1), 2)]); b <- c(0, p[seq(2, 2 * (K - 1), 2)])
    eta <- a + z * b; e <- exp(eta - max(eta)); e / sum(e)
  }
  p0 <- t(apply(draws, 1, probs, z = 0))         # B x K
  p1 <- t(apply(draws, 1, probs, z = 1))
  q <- function(M) apply(M, 2, quantile, c(.025, .5, .975))
  list(
    z0 = q(p0), z1 = q(p1),
    delta = apply(p1 - p0, 2, quantile, c(.025, .5, .975))
  )
}
```

## Table 1 — Class enumeration

Fits 2- to 10-class models with sex as the concomitant, 4,000 starts per
model and 1,000 bootstrap replicates per LRT comparison. In reuse mode, the
verified saved enumeration table is loaded without repeating estimation.

```{r}
#| label: enumeration
#| results: "hold"
#| cache: false
#| class-output: enumeration-scroll
# Report chunks always run. Only explicitly validated measurement results are reused.
n_lca <- nrow(d_lca)
if (reuse_measurement) {
  fit_tbl <- saved_measurement$fit_tbl
  nboot <- if (is.null(saved_measurement$nboot)) 1000L else saved_measurement$nboot
  cat("Reusing saved measurement estimates; no LCA or BLRT refitted.\n")
} else {
item_f <- as.formula(paste0("item(", paste(vars$items, collapse = ", "), ") ~ sex_woman"))
Kmax <- 10

## ---- Parallel backend -------------------------------------------------
## glca/gofglca are single-threaded, so on a multi-core machine the default
## (sequential) enumeration leaves ~all cores idle. We distribute the work
## ourselves across multisession workers: the k-model fits run concurrently,
## and the bootstrap LRT is split into (k x chunk) tasks so the 1000 replicates
## of EACH comparison genuinely span >= nchunks cores (see the BLRT block below).
## >= 8 workers as requested; capped at 16 to keep RAM in check (each worker is
## a separate R process holding its own copy of d_lca). gc() is called after the
## fits, after the bootstrap, and inside every worker once its chunk is done.
## detectCores() can return NA on some platforms/containers; fall back safely so
## n_workers is never NA (which would make plan() error and cascade-fail the run).
n_phys <- parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)
if (is.na(n_phys)) n_phys <- parallel::detectCores()
if (is.na(n_phys)) n_phys <- 4L
n_workers <- max(8L, min(n_phys - 2L, 16L))
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = n_workers)
message("Parallel enumeration on ", n_workers, " workers.")

## Fit 2..Kmax class models concurrently (fits[[1]] stays NULL).
## n.init = n_init (4000) random starts per model avoid local maxima. Two
## worker-side safeguards are needed precisely BECAUSE n.init is large:
##  (1) RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister"): furrr_options(seed = TRUE) switches each
##      worker to the L'Ecuyer-CMRG generator. glca() reseeds internally with
##      set.seed(seed), so under L'Ecuyer its 4000 random starts DIFFER from the
##      (validated) Mersenne-Twister ones -- and for the largest model (k = 10)
##      one L'Ecuyer start is degenerate: loglik -> NaN -> maxdiff -> NA ->
##      glca() errors with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE is needed". Forcing MT
##      makes every worker reproduce the well-behaved standalone fit. (This is
##      why n.init = 10 never failed: 10 starts didn't reach the bad one.)
##  (2) seed fallback 2125 -> 2126 -> ...: belt-and-suspenders. If some future
##      glca version / dataset still seeds a degenerate start, retry with the next
##      seed rather than crash the whole render. 2125 (the lucky seed) is used
##      whenever it works; with the MT fix above it works for every k here, so no
##      fallback is triggered and results stay exactly reproducible at 2125.
## n_init, item_f and d_lca are captured automatically as globals by furrr.
fits <- vector("list", Kmax)
fits[2:Kmax] <- furrr::future_map(2:Kmax, function(k) {
  RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister")
  g <- NULL
  for (s in 2125:2134) {
    g <- tryCatch(glca(item_f, data = d_lca, nclass = k, seed = s,
                       n.init = n_init, verbose = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(g)) break
  }
  if (is.null(g)) stop("glca failed for nclass=", k, " across fallback seeds 2125-2134.")
  attr(g, "successful_seed") <- s
  g
}, .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = TRUE, packages = "glca"))
gc()   # reclaim memory used while collecting the fits back to the main process

## Extract posterior matrix from a glca object (single group).
get_post <- function(g) {
  p <- g$posterior
  if (is.list(p)) p <- p[[1]]
  as.matrix(p)
}

## Defensive getter for gof scalars (slot names vary slightly by glca version;
## if these return NA, inspect str(fits[[4]]$gof) and adjust the candidates).
gof_get <- function(g, what) {
  gg <- g$gof
  cand <- switch(what,
    loglik = c("loglik", "logLik", "ll"),
    aic    = c("aic", "AIC"),
    bic    = c("bic", "BIC"))
  for (nm in cand) if (!is.null(gg[[nm]])) return(as.numeric(gg[[nm]])[1])
  NA_real_
}

n_lca <- nrow(d_lca)
fit_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(2:Kmax, function(k) {
  g  <- fits[[k]]
  ll  <- gof_get(g, "loglik"); aic <- gof_get(g, "aic"); bic <- gof_get(g, "bic")
  np  <- (aic + 2 * ll) / 2                       # npar = (AIC + 2*logL)/2
  caic  <- -2 * ll + np * (log(n_lca) + 1)
  sabic <- -2 * ll + np * log((n_lca + 2) / 24)
  ## AWE (approximate weight of evidence; Banfield & Raftery 1993, Masyn 2013):
  ## -2logL + 2*npar*(3/2 + ln n). Like BIC/CAIC/SABIC, LOWER = better. (See the
  ## table note for the formula variant; this is the psychometric-standard one.)
  awe   <- -2 * ll + 2 * np * (1.5 + log(n_lca))
  post  <- get_post(g); modal <- max.col(post)
  ent   <- relative_entropy(post)
  ## Smallest class + AvePP from MODAL (most-likely) class membership.
  cl_n  <- as.integer(table(factor(modal, levels = 1:k)))      # modal class sizes
  avepp <- vapply(1:k, function(t)                             # AvePP_t per class
             if (any(modal == t)) mean(post[modal == t, t]) else NA_real_, numeric(1))
  tibble::tibble(Classes = k, logLik = ll, npar = np,
                 AIC = aic, BIC = bic, CAIC = caic, SABIC = sabic, AWE = awe,
                 Entropy = ent, `Mean AvePP` = mean(avepp, na.rm = TRUE),
                 `Smallest n` = min(cl_n), `Smallest %` = min(cl_n) / n_lca * 100)
})

## Approximate Bayes factor BF_{k,k+1} = exp((BIC_{k+1} - BIC_k)/2) (Masyn 2013):
## BF > 1 favours the k-class model over k+1 (>3 moderate, >10 strong evidence);
## undefined (NA) for the largest model, which has no k+1. Formatted at display.
bic_next  <- fit_tbl$BIC[match(fit_tbl$Classes + 1L, fit_tbl$Classes)]
fit_tbl$BF <- exp((bic_next - fit_tbl$BIC) / 2)

## ---- Bootstrap LRT, k vs k-1, parallelised across the 1000 replicates ----
## Approach B. Each comparison's nboot=1000 reps are split into `nchunks`
## independent chunks (distinct seeds); chunks for ALL k-comparisons are flat-
## mapped onto the workers (8 k x nchunks tasks), so the 1000 reps genuinely run
## across >=8 cores instead of one. Validated against gofglca on gss08: the
## p-value = mean(boot.GsqR >= observed Deviance) reproduces glca exactly, and
## pooling independent-seed chunks is statistically identical to one long run
## (the reps are i.i.d.). Per-chunk extractor pulls the observed LRT statistic
## from dtable[2,"Deviance"] and the bootstrap LRT vector from boot$boot.GsqR.
nboot   <- 1000
nchunks <- 8L                                  # >=8 -> the 1000 reps span >=8 cores per k
chunk_nb <- rep(nboot %/% nchunks, nchunks)    # reps per chunk (sums to nboot)
rem <- nboot %% nchunks; if (rem) chunk_nb[seq_len(rem)] <- chunk_nb[seq_len(rem)] + 1L

## Flat task grid: one row per (k-comparison, chunk). Distinct seed per chunk.
blrt_grid <- expand.grid(k = 3:Kmax, chunk = seq_len(nchunks), KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)

blrt_chunk <- function(k, chunk, nb, seed) {
  go <- tryCatch(glca::gofglca(fits[[k - 1]], fits[[k]], test = "boot",
                               nboot = nb, seed = seed),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(go)) return(list(k = k, obs = NA_real_, boot = numeric(0)))
  out <- list(k = k,
              obs  = as.numeric(go$dtable[2, "Deviance"]),        # observed LRT stat
              boot = as.numeric(go$boot$boot.GsqR[1, ]))          # bootstrap LRT reps
  rm(go); gc(verbose = FALSE)                  # free per-chunk memory inside worker
  out
}

chunk_res <- furrr::future_pmap(
  list(k = blrt_grid$k, chunk = blrt_grid$chunk),
  ## Unique seed per (k, chunk) -> every comparison draws an independent
  ## bootstrap stream (avoids correlated Monte-Carlo error across k).
  function(k, chunk) blrt_chunk(k, chunk, chunk_nb[chunk],
                                seed = (k - 3L) * nchunks + chunk),
  .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = TRUE, packages = "glca",
                                  globals = c("fits", "chunk_nb", "nchunks", "blrt_chunk")))
future::plan(future::sequential)               # release workers
gc()                                           # tidy the main process

## Pool the chunks back per k and compute p = mean(pooled boot >= observed).
## obs (observed Deviance) is deterministic and identical across a k's chunks,
## so take it from the first chunk that succeeded (not strictly parts[[1]], which
## would drop the whole k if only that one chunk hit a transient failure).
blrt_p <- c(NA, sapply(3:Kmax, function(kk) {
  parts <- chunk_res[vapply(chunk_res, function(z) z$k, numeric(1)) == kk]
  obs   <- stats::na.omit(vapply(parts, function(z) z$obs, numeric(1)))[1]
  boot  <- unlist(lapply(parts, `[[`, "boot"))
  if (is.na(obs) || !length(boot)) NA_real_ else mean(boot >= obs)
}))
fit_tbl$`BLRT P` <- blrt_p[match(fit_tbl$Classes, 2:Kmax)]
rm(chunk_res); gc()
}

fit_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(logLik, AIC, BIC, CAIC, SABIC, AWE), ~round(.x, 2)),
                Entropy = round(Entropy, 3),
                `Mean AvePP` = round(`Mean AvePP`, 3),
                `Smallest %` = round(`Smallest %`, 1),
                BF = dplyr::case_when(is.na(BF)  ~ NA_character_,
                                      BF > 100   ~ ">100",
                                      BF < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
                                      TRUE       ~ sprintf("%.2f", BF)),
                `BLRT P` = ifelse(`BLRT P` < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", `BLRT P`))) |>
  dplyr::select(Classes, logLik, npar, AIC, BIC, CAIC, SABIC, AWE, Entropy,
                `Mean AvePP`, `Smallest n`, `Smallest %`, BF, `BLRT P`) |>
  knitr::kable("markdown", caption = "Table 1. Latent class model fit (2-10 classes; sex as covariate).")
```

*Notes.* **AWE** = approximate weight of evidence criterion, computed as
$-2\log L + 2\,p\,(3/2 + \ln n)$ where $p$ = number of parameters (Banfield &
Raftery, 1993; Masyn, 2013); like BIC/CAIC/SABIC, **lower = better**. (Some
sources drop the factor 2, i.e. $-2\log L + p(3/2 + \ln n)$, or use the
classification log-likelihood; the value above uses the psychometric-standard
form and the observed log-likelihood.) **BF** = approximate Bayes factor
comparing the $k$-class model with the $(k{+}1)$-class model,
$\exp[(\mathrm{BIC}_{k+1}-\mathrm{BIC}_k)/2]$ (Masyn, 2013); $\mathrm{BF} > 1$
favours the more parsimonious $k$-class solution ($>3$ moderate, $>10$ strong),
and it is undefined for the 10-class model (no $k{+}1$). **Mean AvePP** = mean
across classes of the average posterior probability of the modal class
($>.70$ = good separation). **Smallest n / Smallest %** = size of the smallest
class under modal (most-likely) assignment. **Entropy** = relative entropy
($0$–$1$; higher = cleaner classification). The Vuong–Lo–Mendell–Rubin adjusted
LRT is not reported (it cannot be computed reliably from the `glca` output); the
parametric bootstrap LRT (**BLRT P**), found more accurate for LCA class
enumeration by Nylund et al. (2007), is reported instead.

## Four-class model — item-response probabilities (Table 3) and Figure 2

`item_meta` carries the English label and the behavior **type** for each item.
Note **item 3** (`lid_des3`, the negatively worded *laissez-faire* item *"steers
away from showing concern about results"*) is **excluded** from the LCA, so the
measurement model and every figure below are built on the remaining 13 items.

```{r}
#| label: four-class-rho
#| results: "hold"

K <- 4
class_labels <- c("C1 Moderately constructive", "C2 Disengaged",
                  "C3 Constructive", "C4 Ambivalent")
if (reuse_measurement) {
  post4 <- saved_measurement$post4
  rho <- saved_measurement$rho4
  perm <- saved_measurement$class_permutation
  modal4 <- max.col(post4, ties.method = "first")
  sizes <- vapply(1:K, function(k) sum(d_lca$.w[modal4 == k]), numeric(1))
  sizes <- sizes/sum(sizes)
  stopifnot(nrow(post4) == nrow(d_lca))
} else {
g4 <- fits[[4]]
post4 <- get_post(g4)
modal4 <- max.col(post4, ties.method = "first")

## Guard: post4/modal4 must align row-for-row with d_lca (and the survey design
## and all covariate vectors). If glca dropped rows (e.g. concomitant NA), stop
## loudly instead of silently corrupting Tables 2 / S1 / S2 / S3.
stopifnot(nrow(post4) == nrow(d_lca))

## class sizes (weighted share)
sizes <- sapply(1:K, function(t) sum(d_lca$.w[modal4 == t])) ; sizes <- sizes / sum(sizes)

## Item-response probabilities rho: list over items, each K x 4 (categories).
get_rho <- function(g) {
  r <- g$param$rho
  if (is.list(r) && is.list(r[[1]])) r <- r[[1]]   # unwrap group level if present
  r
}
rho <- get_rho(g4)   # rho[[item]] is a K x 4 matrix (rows = class, cols = category)

## ── Canonical class ordering ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## glca does not guarantee consistent class-index ordering across re-renders.
## We enforce a canonical ordering that is stable across runs:
##   C1 = Moderately constructive  C2 = Disengaged
##   C3 = Constructive             C4 = Ambivalent
##
## Algorithm (item profiles only — no covariates, avoids circularity):
##   mean P(response ∈ {3,4}) across all 13 items per class:
##     minimum  → Disengaged (low endorsement across domains)
##     maximum  → Constructive (highest overall endorsement)
##     2nd min  → Ambivalent (mixed; lower overall than constructive)
##     remaining → Moderately constructive
m_top2 <- vapply(1:K, function(k)
  mean(sapply(rho, function(r) r[k, 3] + r[k, 4])), numeric(1))
k_PA <- which.min(m_top2)
k_AC <- which.max(m_top2)
rem  <- setdiff(1:K, c(k_PA, k_AC))
k_AD <- rem[which.min(m_top2[rem])]
k_C  <- setdiff(rem, k_AD)
perm <- c(k_C, k_PA, k_AC, k_AD)   # perm[i] = glca index for canonical slot i
cat("Canonical class mapping (glca index → canonical label):\n")
for (i in 1:4) cat(sprintf("  glca C%d (m_top2=%.3f) → %s\n",
                            perm[i], m_top2[perm[i]], class_labels[i]))
## Apply permutation to all class-indexed objects
post4  <- post4[, perm]
modal4 <- max.col(post4, ties.method = "first")                          # recompute from reordered posteriors
rho    <- lapply(rho, function(r) r[perm, , drop = FALSE])
sizes  <- sapply(1:K, function(t) sum(d_lca$.w[modal4 == t])); sizes <- sizes / sum(sizes)
cat("Class sizes after canonicalization:", paste(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100*sizes), collapse=", "), "\n")
}

## ---- item metadata (order = vars$items = lid_des1..14 WITHOUT lid_des3) --
## lid_des3 is excluded from the LCA (see the variable-mapping chunk), so it is
## intentionally absent here too; this table must stay aligned row-for-row with
## vars$items (13 rows) so rho[[j]] maps to the right item.
item_meta <- tibble::tribble(
  ~item,        ~label,                                          ~type,
  "lid_des1",   "Humiliates employees",                          "Destructive",
  "lid_des2",   "Encourages creative ideas",                     "Constructive",
  "lid_des4",   "Gestures of displeasure",                       "Destructive",
  "lid_des5",   "Avoids making decisions",                       "Laissez-faire",
  "lid_des6",   "Recognizes good performance",                   "Constructive",
  "lid_des7",   "Avoids involvement in work",                    "Laissez-faire",
  "lid_des8",   "Spreads false information",                     "Destructive",
  "lid_des9",   "Absent when needed",                            "Laissez-faire",
  "lid_des10",  "Berates by phone / rude email",                 "Destructive",
  "lid_des11",  "Seeks to develop capabilities",                 "Constructive",
  "lid_des12",  "Sets clear objectives",                         "Constructive",
  "lid_des13",  "Defines / explains tasks",                      "Constructive",
  "lid_des14",  "Flexible, open to innovation",                  "Constructive"
)
behavior_text <- c(Destructive = "Tyrannical", `Laissez-faire` = "*laissez-faire*",
                   Constructive = "Constructive")
behavior_labels <- c(Destructive = "'Tyrannical'", `Laissez-faire` = "italic('laissez-faire')",
                     Constructive = "'Constructive'")
behavior_labeller <- ggplot2::as_labeller(behavior_labels, default = ggplot2::label_parsed)

## ---- Table 3: probability of the top two categories (3 + 4) ------------
top2 <- t(vapply(seq_along(vars$items), function(j) rho[[j]][, 3] + rho[[j]][, 4], numeric(K)))
colnames(top2) <- paste0("C", 1:K)
tab3 <- dplyr::bind_cols(item_meta[, c("label","type")], as.data.frame(round(top2, 2)))

tab3 |>
  dplyr::transmute(`Leadership item` = paste0(label, " (", tolower(behavior_text[type]), ")"),
                   C1, C2, C3, C4) |>
  knitr::kable("markdown", caption = "Table 3. Item-response probabilities (categories 3+4), four-class model.")
```

```{r}
#| label: figure2
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| results: "hold"

cats <- c("Never","Sometimes","Fairly often","Almost always/always")
blue <- c("#DEEBF7","#9ECAE1","#4292C6","#08519C")

rho_long <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(vars$items), function(j) {
  m <- rho[[j]]                                   # K x 4
  tidyr::expand_grid(class = 1:K, cat = 1:4) |>
    dplyr::mutate(p = as.vector(t(m))[ (class-1)*4 + cat ],
                  item = item_meta$item[j])
}) |>

fig2 <- ggplot(rho_long, aes(p, label, fill = cat)) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = blue, name = "Response category") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     breaks = c(0, .5, 1), expand = expansion(mult = .04)) +
  labs(x = "Response-category probability", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.spacing.x = unit(1, "lines"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 0))
fig2
ggsave("Figure2_itemprob.png", fig2, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Classification diagnostics — AvePP and OCC

For the retained four-class model, classification quality is summarised by the
**average posterior probability** (AvePP) and the **odds of correct
classification** (OCC). AvePP$_k$ is the mean posterior probability of class $k$
among the cases modally assigned to class $k$ (rule of thumb: AvePP $>$ .70 for
every class). OCC$_k = [\text{AvePP}_k/(1-\text{AvePP}_k)] \big/ [\pi_k/(1-\pi_k)]$,
where $\pi_k$ is the estimated class prevalence (mean posterior); OCC$_k > 5$
indicates good assignment (Nagin, 2005).

```{r}
#| label: avepp-occ
#| results: "hold"

Kd      <- ncol(post4)
pi_k    <- colMeans(post4)                                   # estimated prevalence
n_modal <- as.integer(table(factor(modal4, levels = 1:Kd)))  # modal class sizes
AvePP   <- vapply(1:Kd, function(k) mean(post4[modal4 == k, k]), numeric(1))
OCC     <- (AvePP / (1 - AvePP)) / (pi_k / (1 - pi_k))

class_diag <- tibble::tibble(
  Class               = paste0("C", 1:Kd),
  `n (modal)`         = n_modal,
  `pi_k (prevalence)` = round(pi_k, 3),
  AvePP               = round(AvePP, 3),
  OCC                 = round(OCC, 2)
)
class_diag |>
  knitr::kable("markdown",
    caption = "Classification diagnostics (four-class): average posterior probabilities (AvePP) and odds of correct classification (OCC).")
```

```{r}
#| label: avepp-results-sentence
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
ent4  <- relative_entropy(post4)
all70 <- all(AvePP > 0.70)
cat(sprintf(
  "All four profiles are assigned with high certainty: average posterior probabilities range %.2f to %.2f%s, and odds of correct classification exceed %.0f for every class, consistent with the high relative entropy (%.2f). Classification error is therefore minimal.\n",
  min(AvePP), max(AvePP),
  if (all70) " (all > .70)" else " (note: not all exceed .70)",
  floor(min(OCC)), ent4))
```



## Medians (Q1–Q3) and Table 2 — survey-weighted profile characteristics

Continuous variables are summarized as survey-weighted median (Q1-Q3), and
binary characteristics as survey-weighted percentages. Participant counts are
unweighted. P-values are global comparisons across the four fixed modal classes:
Rao-Scott F tests for binary characteristics and survey-adjusted Kruskal-Wallis
rank tests for continuous characteristics. The latter compare ranks/distributions,
not exclusively medians. SMD is the maximum absolute standardized mean difference
among the six class pairs, using weighted means and class-specific variances.
It is not a standardized difference of medians. These descriptive comparisons
condition on modal classification and do not correct classification uncertainty.

```{r}
#| label: table2
#| results: "hold"

bin_vars <- c(
  "Unpaid care work at home -- yes" = "unpaid_care",
  "Did not complete secondary school" = "no_secondary",
  "Absence of union -- yes" = "no_union",
  "Workplace 1-10 workers" = "small_wp",
  "Customer-facing tasks -- no" = "customer_no",
  "Economic narrowness -- yes" = "econ_narrow",
  "Effort-reward imbalance -- yes" = "eri",
  "Sex -- women" = "sex_woman",
  "Hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT-C) -- yes" = "auditc_hazard",
  "Frequent negative acts (NAQ) -- yes" = "naq_frequent",
  "Self-labeled bullying (last 6 mo)" = "bully_self",
  "Sexual harassment (last 12 mo)" = "sex_harass",
  "Psychotropic medication use -- yes" = "psychotrop_flexible")
stopifnot(sum(d_lca$psychotrop_flexible == 1, na.rm = TRUE) == 247L,
          sum(is.na(d_lca$psychotrop_flexible)) == 8L)
table2 <- build_leadership_table2(dsn, modal4, post4, class_labels, bin_vars)
## Yang-Dalton max |SMD| over the six class pairs, also without weights, with the
## pair attaining each maximum (same method as table2_smd_recalculado.R).
table2_unweighted <- build_leadership_table2(
  svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = rep(1, nrow(d_lca)), data = d_lca),
  modal4, post4, class_labels, bin_vars)
smd_max <- function(pairs, suffix) {
  out <- dplyr::slice_max(dplyr::group_by(pairs, variable), abs_smd, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::transmute(variable, max_abs_smd = abs_smd, pair = paste(class_a, "vs", class_b))
  stats::setNames(out, c("variable", paste0(c("max_abs_smd_", "pair_"), suffix)))
}
table2_smd_max <- dplyr::inner_join(smd_max(table2$smd_pairs, "weighted"),
                                    smd_max(table2_unweighted$smd_pairs, "unweighted"), by = "variable")
table2_smd_max <- table2_smd_max[match(table2$tests$variable, table2_smd_max$variable), ]
stopifnot(identical(table2_smd_max$variable, table2$tests$variable),
          isTRUE(all.equal(table2_smd_max$max_abs_smd_weighted, table2$tests$max_abs_smd)))
t2_full <- table2$full; t2_bin <- table2$binary; t2_cont <- table2$continuous
data_rows <- match(table2$tests$characteristic, t2_full$Characteristic)
t2_full$`SMD pair` <- t2_full$`SMD unweighted` <- t2_full$`SMD unweighted pair` <- ""
t2_full$`SMD pair`[data_rows] <- table2_smd_max$pair_weighted
t2_full$`SMD unweighted`[data_rows] <- sprintf("%.2f", table2_smd_max$max_abs_smd_unweighted)
t2_full$`SMD unweighted pair`[data_rows] <- table2_smd_max$pair_unweighted
t2_full <- t2_full[, c("Characteristic", paste0("C", 1:4), "P", "SMD", "SMD pair",
                       "SMD unweighted", "SMD unweighted pair")]
## Manuscript headers (442/303/559/559) are rounded sums of weights, not people.
weight_row <- t2_full[1, ]; weight_row[] <- ""
weight_row$Characteristic <- "Sum of survey weights"
weight_row[paste0("C", 1:4)] <- as.list(sprintf("%.0f", table2$class_sizes$weight_sum))
t2_full <- rbind(t2_full[1, ], weight_row, t2_full[-1, ])
t2_full |> knitr::kable("html", caption = "Table 2. Survey-weighted characteristics by leadership profile.")
table2$class_sizes |> knitr::kable("html", digits = 3,
  caption = "Class-size audit: actual participants, sum of weights, weighted modal share, and model prevalence.")
```

*Notes.* Counts are unweighted; percentages and medians (Q1-Q3) are survey-weighted.
The design uses weights only because strata and PSU identifiers are not mapped.
For each variable, estimates exclude its missing values; the exported numeric
summary gives every nonmissing denominator. Weighted quantiles retain midpoint
weighted-ECDF interpolation from the original notebook. For a pair of classes,
SMD = $(\mu_a-\mu_b)/\sqrt{(v_a+v_b)/2}$, where continuous $v$ is the survey
estimate of population variance and binary $v=p(1-p)$. All six contrasts are
exported, including signs; the maximum is also reported without weights, each
with the class pair that attains it. P-values are exploratory and are not multiplicity-adjusted.
Unavailable tests are labeled "Not estimable" with a reason in the test export.
See the [survey rank-test documentation](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/survey/html/svyranktest.html).

## Table S1 — ML three-step odds ratios (reference = C1 Constructive)

One covariate at a time. Each row is the per-class OR (vs C1 Constructive) for a
one-unit change in the covariate, from the from-scratch `ml3step()`.

```{r}
#| label: tableS1
#| results: "hold"
#| cache: false
## cache OFF: ml3step is cheap (seconds), and a cached tableS1 would silently keep
## stale odds ratios if ml3step() or post4/modal4 change upstream (knitr cache keys
## only on this chunk's own code, not on upstream objects).

## covariates to model (label -> key); reference class is C1
or_vars <- c(
  "Effort-reward imbalance"        = "eri",
  "Hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT-C)"= "auditc_hazard",
  "Absence of union"               = "no_union",
  "Frequent negative acts (NAQ)"   = "naq_frequent",
  "Self-labeled bullying"          = "bully_self",
  "Sexual harassment"              = "sex_harass",
  "Female sex"                     = "sex_woman"
)

fit_or <- function(key) {
  ml3step(z = d_lca[[key]], post = post4, modal = modal4, sw = d_lca$.w)
}
ml_models <- lapply(or_vars, fit_or)

s1 <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  m <- ml_models[[lab]]
  if (is.null(m)) stop("Missing ML model for ", key)
  fmt <- function(i) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", m$ors$OR[i], m$ors$lo[i], m$ors$hi[i])
  tibble::tibble(Covariate = lab,
                 `C2 vs C1` = fmt(1), `C3 vs C1` = fmt(2), `C4 vs C1` = fmt(3))
})
s1 |> knitr::kable("markdown", caption = "Table S1. ML three-step odds ratios (95% CI), reference = C1.")
```

## Table S2 — Marginal predicted probabilities by covariate level

Predicted P(class | covariate) at *No* (z = 0) and *Yes* (z = 1), with parametric
bootstrap 95% CIs and the difference Δ (pp), from the same ML three-step fits.

```{r}
#| label: tableS2
#| results: "hold"

cls_lab <- class_labels
set.seed(2125)  # Same intervals whether enumeration is reused or refitted.
margin_objects <- lapply(ml_models, ml3step_margins)
s2 <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  m <- ml_models[[lab]]
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  mg <- margin_objects[[lab]]
  purrr::map_dfr(1:4, function(t) tibble::tibble(
    Covariate = ifelse(t == 1, lab, ""),
    Profile   = cls_lab[t],
    `No, % (95% CI)`  = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", 100*mg$z0[2,t], 100*mg$z0[1,t], 100*mg$z0[3,t]),
    `Yes, % (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", 100*mg$z1[2,t], 100*mg$z1[1,t], 100*mg$z1[3,t]),
    `Delta (pp)`      = sprintf("%+.1f", 100*mg$delta[2,t])
  ))
})
s2 |> knitr::kable("markdown", caption = "Table S2. Marginal predicted probabilities by covariate level.")
```

## Table S3 — Sensitivity analysis: naive vs BCH

This existing sensitivity uses unweighted estimates in both methods.
For each binary covariate, the class-specific prevalence (and the mean of job
satisfaction) under **naive modal assignment** versus **BCH** bias-adjustment.
The maximum absolute naive–BCH discrepancy quantifies the impact of
classification error (small when entropy is high).

```{r}
#| label: tableS3
#| results: "hold"

bch <- bch_setup(post4, modal4)

s3_vars <- c(
  "Effort-reward imbalance"        = "eri",
  "Self-labeled bullying"          = "bully_self",
  "Frequent negative acts (NAQ)"   = "naq_frequent",
  "Hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT-C)"= "auditc_hazard",
  "Absence of union"               = "no_union",
  "Sexual harassment"             = "sex_harass",
  "Female sex"                    = "sex_woman",
  "Psychotropic medication use"   = "psychotrop_flexible"
)

disc <- c()
s3 <- purrr::imap_dfr(s3_vars, function(key, lab) {
  x  <- d_lca[[key]]
  nv <- naive_class_mean(x, modal4) * 100
  bv <- bch_class_mean(x, bch$w)    * 100
  disc <<- c(disc, max(abs(nv - bv)))
  tibble::tibble(Covariate = lab,
    C1 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[1], bv[1]), C2 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[2], bv[2]),
    C3 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[3], bv[3]), C4 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[4], bv[4]))
})

## job satisfaction: mean (naive / BCH)
{
  js <- d_lca$job_sat
  nv <- naive_class_mean(js, modal4); bv <- bch_class_mean(js, bch$w)
  s3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(s3, tibble::tibble(Covariate = "Job satisfaction, mean",
    C1 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[1], bv[1]), C2 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[2], bv[2]),
    C3 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[3], bv[3]), C4 = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", nv[4], bv[4])))
}

cat(sprintf("Max absolute naive-BCH discrepancy: %.1f pp (%s)\n", suppressWarnings(max(disc)),
            names(s3_vars)[which.max(disc)]))
cat(sprintf("Relative entropy, four classes: %.6f\n", relative_entropy(post4)))
s3 |> knitr::kable("markdown", caption = "Table S3. Sensitivity: class-specific estimates (naive / BCH).")
```
